subtitle: How Stone, Sea and Cunning Turned a Kingdom into a Landscape of Forts

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Raigad fort rising from misty Sahyadri cliffs at dawn
panels.action: Hiroji Indulkar stands on a jagged Raigad bastion overlooking endless Sahyadri ridges and distant sea forts, his hand resting on a survey staff as clouds swirl below the sheer drops.

dialogue.text: This is the age when the Sahyadris grew walls, when Hiroji Indulkar and Maratha engineers turned stone and sea into a living shield.

i18n.hi: वो दौर जब सह्याद्री ने दीवारें उगाईं, जब हिरोजी इंदुलकर और मराठा अभियंताओं ने पत्थर और सागर को जिंदा ढाल बना दिया।

panels.shot: wide aerial over Western Ghats showing Mughal camp in Deccan plains and scattered hill forts on peaks
panels.action: An expansive view shows Mughal tents and artillery on the flat Deccan while, far above, isolated hill-forts cling to the saw-toothed Sahyadri ridges under gathering clouds.

dialogue.text: Seventeenth-century Deccan: great empires march with heavy guns on the plains, but in the broken stone spine of the Sahyadris, power must climb.

i18n.hi: सत्रहवीं सदी का दक्कन: मैदानों पर तोपों से लैस साम्राज्य, पर सह्याद्री की टूटी रीढ़ पर ताकत को चढ़ना पड़ता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hiroji studying a rugged hill with villagers and soldiers around him
panels.action: A younger Hiroji Indulkar in simple turban and angarkha stands with a measuring rope and wooden plumb line, studying a steep hill while local peasants and Maratha soldiers point out paths and ledges.

dialogue.text: Shivaji needs more than bravery. He needs hills that fight. Hiroji Indulkar and other local builders learn to read rock like a book.

i18n.hi: शिवाजी को सिर्फ बहादुरी नहीं चाहिए; उन्हें लड़ने वाली पहाड़ियाँ चाहिए। हिरोजी इंदुलकर और कारीगर चट्टान को किताब की तरह पढ़ना सीखते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Raigad under construction from a mid-distance vantage
panels.action: Raigad rises in stages; labourers haul stones up narrow paths, masons fit black basalt blocks, and Hiroji stands on a half-built bastion, gesturing toward where walls must trace the cliff edge.

dialogue.text: On Raigad’s knife-edge, they do not impose a fortress upon the hill. They coax the hill to become a fortress.

i18n.hi: रायगढ़ की धार पर वो किला थोपते नहीं; पहाड़ को ही धीरे‑धीरे किला बना लेते हैं।

panels.shot: cutaway-style wide shot of Raigad’s approach paths and gateways from above
panels.action: An overhead view reveals Raigad’s winding access: a narrow path hugging a cliff, a steep flight of steps, and a bent entrance-turn where high stone walls conceal the inner way.

dialogue.text: The straight road is a gift to the cannon. So entrances bend, twist, vanish around corners. Each angle robs enemy guns of aim.

i18n.hi: सीधी राह तोपों का तोहफा है। इसलिए दरवाज़े मुड़ते, टूटते, कोनों में गायब हो जाते हैं। हर मोड़ दुश्मन की तोप की नज़र छीन लेता है।

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot of a bent entrance passage with a hidden sally-port
panels.action: Inside a dim stone passage, a tight turn hides a small side door set low in the wall, while above the passage ceiling narrow slits hint at hidden defenders.

dialogue.text: Bent gateways break the rush of men. Tiny sally-ports let a handful dart out, strike, and vanish while the main door stays barred.

i18n.hi: टेढ़े दरवाज़े हमले की रफ़्तार तोड़ते हैं। छोटी सुरंगों से मुट्ठीभर निकलते हैं, वार करते हैं, ग़ायब हो जाते हैं, जबकि बड़ा फाटक बंद ही रहता है।

panels.shot: wide interior courtyard shot of Raigad with cistern and granary in view
panels.action: In Raigad’s inner courtyard, a deep stone cistern filled with dark water sits beside a low, thick-walled granary, while women draw water and soldiers carry sacks of grain under the watch of officers.

dialogue.text: Water and grain are the true walls. Rock-cut cisterns drink the monsoon, and granaries turn siege into waiting.

i18n.hi: असली दीवारें पानी और अनाज हैं। पत्थर काटकर बने कुंड बारिश पीते हैं, और कोठार घेराबंदी को इंतज़ार में बदल देते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot on Hiroji and another engineer marking a rock face for cistern cutting
panels.action: Hiroji and a fellow engineer squat by a sloping rock, scratching lines with chalk and tapping the stone, while workers with iron tools prepare to start cutting a tank.

dialogue.speaker: hiroji_indulkar_and_maratha_engineers
dialogue.text: Cut deep, brothers. If the sky betrays us, the stone must not.

i18n.hi: गहरा काटो, भाइयों। अगर आसमान धोखा दे, तो पत्थर नहीं देना चाहिए।

panels.shot: wide sweeping shot of multiple forts across Sahyadris connected visually by ridgelines
panels.action: A panoramic view shows Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad and distant hill-forts perched on different peaks, ridgelines and valleys linking them like a broken chain through the mist.

dialogue.text: Over decades, more peaks bristle with stone—Rajgad, Pratapgad, Torna. Each hill is a tooth, each ridge a jaw in a loose, growing chain.

i18n.hi: सालों में और चोटियाँ पत्थर से सजीं—राजगढ़, प्रतापगढ़, तोरणा। हर पहाड़ी दाँत, हर पहाड़ी शृंखला ढीली, फैलती हुई जबान।

panels.shot: wide coastal shot of Sindhudurg sea fort as seen from a small Maratha warship
panels.action: From the deck of a small sail-driven Maratha vessel, Sindhudurg’s low, massive sea walls rise directly from the Arabian Sea, blending with the rocky island as waves crash at their base.

dialogue.text: Where the Sahyadris fall into the sea, stone marches on. Sindhudurg, Suvarnadurg, Vijaydurg: forts not on hills, but in the surf.

i18n.hi: जहाँ सह्याद्री समंदर में गिरते हैं, वहाँ भी पत्थर आगे बढ़ता है। सिंधुदुर्ग, सुवर्णदुर्ग, विजयदुर्ग: किले जो पहाड़ पर नहीं, लहरों के बीच हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot from within Sindhudurg walls looking out to anchored ships and reef
panels.action: Standing atop Sindhudurg’s wall, Maratha officers point to submerged rocky reefs that force hostile ships into narrow channels, while small armed boats rest ready below.

dialogue.text: Here, the reef is a ditch, the tide a moat. Channels twist like hill paths, turning foreign hulls into targets for lighter Maratha craft.

i18n.hi: यहाँ रीफ़ ही खाई है, ज्वार ही खंदक। नाले पहाड़ी पगडंडियों की तरह मुड़ते हैं, परदेसी जहाज़ों को हल्की मराठी नौकाओं का शिकार बना देते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Vijaydurg’s projecting sea bastion and inner harbour at sunset
panels.action: At sunset, Vijaydurg’s long sea bastion stretches into the water, enclosing a calm inner harbour where a few ships lie at anchor, dwarfed by massive curtain walls.

dialogue.text: Vijaydurg’s arm reaches into the sea, cupping a harbour in stone. The Maratha state breathes through these inlets when plains are aflame.

i18n.hi: विजयदुर्ग की बाँह समंदर में बढ़ती है, पत्थर की हथेली में लंगरगाह थामे। मैदानों में आग हो तो मराठा राज्य इन्हीं घाटों से साँस लेता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a messenger arriving at Raigad with scrolls while engineers listen
panels.action: A dusty horseman hands scrolls to a court official in Raigad’s courtyard while Hiroji and fellow engineers stand nearby, their expressions alert as they sense threat in the hurried arrival.

dialogue.text: From the north comes word of Aurangzeb’s grinding war. For a smaller kingdom, the forts must be lungs, moving people, grain, messages between hill and sea.

i18n.hi: उत्तर से औरंगज़ेब की थकाने वाली जंग की खबर आती है। छोटे राज्य के लिए किले ही फेफड़े बनते हैं—लोग, अनाज, संदेश पहाड़ और सागर के बीच बहते रहते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mughal army camped below a steep fort, smoke rising from campfires
panels.action: On the plain below a high fort, rows of Mughal tents, elephants, and artillery form a spreading camp, the fort above silhouetted dark against storm clouds.

dialogue.text: Many times, imperial camps ring these cliffs. Cannon thunder, banners snap, but walls cling to rock, and supplies creep by night along goat paths.

i18n.hi: कई बार शाही डेरों ने इन चट्टानों को घेरा। तोपें गरजीं, झंडे फड़फड़ाए, पर दीवारें पत्थर से चिपकी रहीं और रसद बकरियों की पगडंडियों से रात में सरकती रही।

panels.shot: medium shot of Maratha defenders at a hidden postern gate leading to a steep path
panels.action: Inside the fort’s shadowed inner wall, a small group of Maratha soldiers slip through a low postern gate, emerging onto a steep, narrow track that winds down into forest darkness.

dialogue.text: Hidden back-gates and forest tracks carry men and news out even when main gates are silent under siege.

i18n.hi: छिपे पिछवाड़े के दरवाज़े और जंगलों की पगडंडियाँ आदमी और खबरें निकालती रहती हैं, जब मुख्य फाटक घेराबंदी में खामोश रहता है।

panels.shot: close-up on a British officer’s face writing by lamplight, parchment and quill visible
panels.action: By the dim glow of an oil lamp, an English officer representing Henry Oxienden bends over parchment, his brow furrowed, quill scratching as he records impressions of Raigad’s defenses.

dialogue.text: In 1674, Henry Oxienden, an English visitor, writes of Raigad’s steep approaches and stores with wary respect. Foreign eyes measure what local masons have wrought.

i18n.hi: १६७४ में अंग्रेज़ यात्री हेनरी ऑक्सिंडन रायगढ़ की खड़ी चढ़ाइयों और भंडार पर सतर्क सम्मान से लिखता है। पराई निगाहें आँकती हैं जो देशी राजमिस्त्रियों ने गढ़ा।

panels.shot: wide shot of a map table with Deccan and Konkan coasts marked, engineers placing tokens for forts
panels.action: Hiroji and later-generation engineers stand over a rough cloth map of the Deccan and Konkan coast, placing small stone tokens where forts stand on hills and along the shore.

dialogue.text: Over time, commanders and engineers think in chains and clusters. Hill holds valley, valley feeds coast, coast opens to sea. Not a single grand plan, but habit, memory, adaptation.

i18n.hi: धीरे‑धीरे सरदार और अभियंता झुंड और ज़ंजीर में सोचने लगते हैं। पहाड़ी घाट पकड़ती है, घाट तट को खिलाती है, तट समंदर खोलता है। कोई एक बड़ा नक्शा नहीं, पर आदत, याद, और ढलते रहना।

panels.shot: melancholic wide shot of Raigad in later, decayed state with vegetation on walls
panels.action: Years later, Raigad’s once-busy courtyards lie quiet; grass grows between stone steps, some walls lie broken, yet cisterns still reflect the sky and the bastions still cling to the cliff.

dialogue.text: By 1818, the Maratha polity falls to another empire. Many forts are broken, their guns silenced, but their bones remain in the rock.

i18n.hi: १८१८ तक मराठा सत्ता किसी और साम्राज्य के हाथ गिरती है। कई किले ढहाए जाते हैं, तोपें खामोश हो जाती हैं, पर उनकी हड्डियाँ पत्थर में रह जाती हैं।

panels.shot: modern wide shot of tourists and conservation workers at Raigad with UNESCO-style survey equipment
panels.action: In a present-day scene, conservation workers use survey tripods and notebooks on Raigad’s walls while visitors walk the steps, the vast Sahyadri landscape stretching beyond under a clear sky.

dialogue.text: In 2025, the Maratha Military Landscapes—Raigad, Sindhudurg and more—enter UNESCO’s rolls after debate, as scholars trace how fort and hill, sea and state once breathed together.

i18n.hi: २०२५ में रायगढ़, सिंधुदुर्ग जैसे मराठा सैन्य परिदृश्य बहस के बाद यूनेस्को की सूची में आते हैं, जब विद्वान देखते हैं कैसे किला और पहाड़, सागर और सत्ता एक साथ साँस लेते थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Hiroji’s imagined statue or memorial plaque, with background blur of hills and sea
panels.action: A carved likeness of Hiroji Indulkar on a weathered plaque stands in the foreground, while behind it blurred outlines of hills and distant sea forts hint at the vast landscape his craft shaped.

dialogue.text: These forts show that courage alone is not enough. It is design—cistern and curve, gate and harbour—that lets courage endure long after armies have passed.

i18n.hi: ये किले दिखाते हैं कि सिर्फ जिगर काफी नहीं। वही डिजाइन—कुंड और मोड़, फाटक और बंदरगाह—हिम्मत को उस वक़्त तक ज़िंदा रखता है जब फौजें बहुत पीछे छूट चुकी होती हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Stone, Sea and Cunning Turned a Kingdom into a Landscape of Forts
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर, सागर और चालाकी ने कैसे एक राज्य को किलों की धरती बना दिया
